statement.p: Evaluate the surface integral \int_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \ d \mathbf{S} where \mathbf{F}=5xy\boldsymbol{i}+6x^{2}\boldsymbol{j}+5yz\boldsymbol{k}\ and S is the surface z=xe^y,\ 0 \le x \le 1, 0 \le y \le 1, with upwards orientation.

static.solution: \mathbf{r}(x,y)=(x,y,g(x,y)) where z = g(x,y) = xe^y and D is the square D = [0,1]\times [0,1]. S has upwards orientation, so \int_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \ d \mathbf{S} = \int\int_D ( -5 x y \frac{\delta g}{\delta x} - 6 x^2 \frac{\delta g}{\delta y} + 5 y z)\ dA = \int\int_D (-5 x y e^y - 6 x^3 e^y + 5 y z)\ dA = \int_0^1\int_0^1 (-5 x y e^y - 6 x^3 e^y + 5 x y e^y)\ dy\ dx = \int_0^1 [- 6 x^3 e^y]_0^1\ dx = \int_0^1 - 6 x^3 (e - 1)\ dx = 6(1 - e)\int_0^1 x^3 \ dx = \frac {3} 2 (1-e)
